Introduction

Dokyun, formerly known by the stage name DK, is a South Korean singer currently under DS Entertainment. He was previously a member of the pre-debut boy group DV.OL and the boy group BLANK2Y before embarking on a solo career. He officially debuted as a soloist on April 25, 2025 with the digital single Light On Me.

He first came into the spotlight in early 2022 when Keystone Entertainment revealed him as a member of their upcoming boy group BLANK2Y. On January 7, the company’s CEO hinted at his role as the oldest member of the team, describing him as a “new face.” He was formally introduced on February 26 as the group’s eighth member, and later that year, on May 24, BLANK2Y made their debut with the mini album K2Y I : Confidence [Thumbs Up]. After a little over a year of activities, Dokyun and several members chose to part ways with Keystone Entertainment. On June 27, 2023, he, along with Louis, U, Sungjun, and Sodam, terminated their exclusive contracts. By August 16, the same group of former members had signed with DS Entertainment. Two months later, on October 24, he was announced as part of DS Entertainment’s upcoming boy group DV.OL. However, his path shifted once again in September 2024, when it was revealed that he had departed DV.OL and would prepare instead for a solo debut in the following year.

In April 2025, Dokyun confirmed plans for his first solo release. On April 14, he shared news of his debut single Light On Me, which was officially released on April 25. His solo work continued quickly after: on June 20, he teased his second digital single Better With You, releasing a snippet of the track before its official launch on August 6. Just days later, on August 8, he announced his third single Unbound, which was released on August 13. Outside of music, Dokyun’s health briefly interrupted his career in 2022. Shortly after his debut with BLANK2Y, he underwent emergency surgery for acute appendicitis on May 27 and was placed on temporary rest for two to three weeks. During this time, the group continued promotions with eight members while he focused on recovery.
